title: isolate-gpu-credentials-and-multi-az-subnet-allocator
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce blast radius of GPU nodepool credentials and provide deterministic multi-AZ subnet allocation for Private deployments. This change introduces three coordinated Terraform modules and a small migration helper: 1) modules/gpu/credential_isolation - creates tenant-scoped service accounts / IAM bindings for GPU nodepools so nodepool bootstrap tokens are not shared across tenants; 2) modules/network/multi_az_subnet_allocator - deterministic allocator that assigns nodepools to AZ-specific subnets based on a hash of tenant ID + pool name, allowing predictable AZ affinity and even AZ-distribution in clusters with uneven nodepool counts; 3) modules/state/terraform_state_segmenter - re-layout for tfstate that separates state per-tenant and per-network-scope to simplify rollbacks and reduce state contention. Additional helper: tools/tfstate-segmenter-migrator.sh which is an idempotent migration helper that uses lock-step moves and retains old state references for rollback. Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative in resource naming to avoid switching existing customers automatically; new module inputs are opt-in via cluster_profile.enable_tenant_state_split and cluster_profile.enable_gpu_cred_isolation. The description below is a single narrative describing changes, migration plan, and testing notes. Migration plan: run the migrator in a dry-run mode (tools/tfstate-segmenter-migrator.sh --dry-run) to validate relocation candidates, then coordinate a short maintenance window to move state blobs and apply new modules with enable flags. Rollback: migrator preserves a pointer file (state-pointer-backup.json) and the modules avoid destructive renames by default. Security: the credential isolation module scopes IAM roles to per-tenant service accounts and adds explicit secrets encryption using KMS keys referenced by customers. Backwards compatibility: defaults keep existing behavior; enabling flags are required to opt-in. Impact: expected to reduce cross-tenant credential exposure and improve network determinism for multi-AZ private installs. See linked linear ENG-1208 for performance targets and ENG-1215 for security acceptance criteria.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Strong design. Two asks: (1) can we avoid creating extra IAM roles per tenant when tenant_count == 1 (edge-case cost), (2) add explicit docs on KMS key rotation behavior?

Asha Patel: Responded - added a conditional to skip per-tenant role creation when var.tenant_count == 1 and documented key rotation semantics in the README (see modules/gpu/credential_isolation/README.md).
Lena Brooks: allocator algorithm looks good, but please add an escape hatch for admins to pin a nodepool to a specific AZ (we need this for shop-floor metal).
Asha Patel: Added optional input pinned_az_map and updated examples/private/tenant-isolated-cluster.tf to show usage.
